dossier.bio: Long-time leader of the National Rally (RN), Marine Le Pen has been the party’s central presidential figure in 2012, 2017 and 2022. Her political project has combined a national-sovereignty message with a sustained effort to broaden the party’s appeal beyond its historic base. She announced a 2027 candidacy on 7 July 2026. The legal status of her candidacy must be tracked separately from electoral support and sponsorships; the current source record says her appeal judgment reduced the ineligibility penalty, while further legal steps remain relevant.
dossier.record: Her record includes leading the RN parliamentary group and serving as an MP; she has repeatedly contested presidential elections. The party has moved from the older Front National brand to the RN and pursued a strategy commonly described as normalisation or dédiabolisation. Her programme should not be inferred wholesale from the 2022 manifesto.
themes: Immigration and border controls; national preference and changes to access to public benefits
Purchasing power, household taxation and energy costs
Public order, policing and justice
National sovereignty and a more restrictive approach to aspects of EU integration
Industrial protection and economic nationalism

positions.detail: At the 27 August 2026 MEDEF debate, she defended a return to a legal retirement age of 62, with 60 for qualifying long-career workers and 42 contribution years. The research workbook records a stated full-year cost estimate of €9bn; this is an attributed claim, not an independently validated costing.

At the MEDEF debate she said the RN would present a €125bn savings plan before the autumn budget debate and argued for a rule limiting current-spending deficits. The headline amount needs a line-by-line costing before being treated as a verified saving.

RN themes include reducing production costs and regulations while combining protectionist measures with purchasing-power pledges. Exact 2027 measures and funding should be taken from a published programme, not inferred from party history.

dossier.feasibility: Key tests: whether proposed savings are specified by budget line; compatibility of national-preference measures with French constitutional and EU law; and the interaction between tax cuts, public services and deficit targets.
dossier.open: The final legal status and formal ballot qualification; detailed 2027 programme; complete financing plan; precise legal design of national-preference proposals.
dossier.programme: No complete official 2027 programme was indexed by Observatoire 2027 in its 7 November 2026 programme snapshot. A candidate announcement is not itself a manifesto.

dossier.bio: Founder and leading figure of La France insoumise (LFI), Jean-Luc Mélenchon has served as a senator, minister and MP and has run for president three times (2012, 2017 and 2022). He announced another candidacy on 3 May 2026. On 7 November 2026, LFI presented a written programme at Le Bourget, making this one of the most developed published platforms in the current field.
dossier.record: His political career spans the Socialist Party, the Left Party and LFI. The 2022 presidential campaign and the NUPES alliance shaped his recent national profile. The 2027 programme should be read as the current party platform; earlier LFI plans and parliamentary positions are useful context but are not substitutes for it.
themes: Redistribution, higher wages and stronger public services
Price controls or regulated prices for essential goods
Progressive taxation and greater contributions from high incomes and wealth
Reversing the 2023 pension reform, with a medium-term goal of retirement at 60
Ecological planning and a shift in energy policy away from nuclear
A more non-aligned foreign policy and changes to France’s NATO relationship

positions.detail: The 7 November programme launch was reported by Reuters as pledging a higher minimum wage; the exact implementation and financing should be checked against the full programme text.

At the 27 August MEDEF debate, Mélenchon called for repeal of the 2023 reform, an initial return to 62 and a medium-term objective of 60, with 40 contribution years. The research workbook also records a proposal to raise the minimum old-age benefit and gradually increase pension contributions.

At the MEDEF debate he argued for restructuring public debt, including debt held by the European Central Bank. This is a political proposal whose legal, monetary and market consequences require separate analysis.

dossier.feasibility: Key tests: the fiscal cost and revenue assumptions behind the programme; the legal and institutional route for price controls and debt restructuring; labour-market effects of wage changes; and the practical timetable for energy transition.
dossier.open: Full independent costing; exact timetable and legislative route for the pension rollback; treatment of EU and NATO commitments; detailed sequencing of energy policy.
dossier.programme: A written 2027 programme was presented on 7 November 2026. Observatoire 2027 indexed 142 written commitments across 24 topics and seven documents in its 7 November snapshot. These are party commitments, not independent costings.

dossier.bio: Former prime minister (2017–2020), former mayor of Le Havre and founder of Horizons. Philippe announced his presidential candidacy on 3 September 2024, making him an early declared contender. His political positioning is centre-right and pro-European, with an emphasis on governing competence, economic reform and institutional stability.
dossier.record: As prime minister he oversaw the early Macron presidency, including labour-market reforms, the Yellow Vest crisis, the start of the COVID-19 pandemic and the initial pension-reform attempt. Those government decisions form part of his record but should not be presented as new 2027 pledges unless he renews them.
themes: Fiscal consolidation and debt reduction
Work incentives, competitiveness and labour-market reform
Pension-system sustainability, including a higher retirement age
Public-service and state reform

positions.detail: On 29 September 2026 he argued for raising the legal retirement age to 65 in less than ten years, a 45-year contribution period and a funded pillar. The research workbook records a proposed €500 initial retirement-savings contribution and an estimated €30bn annual yield; these are attributed claims requiring independent scrutiny.
At the time of the MEDEF debate he proposed limiting the maximum unemployment-benefit period to 12 months for people under 50, continuing a direction associated with reforms during his premiership.
At the MEDEF debate he rejected debt cancellation and emphasised restoring balanced public accounts.

dossier.feasibility: Key tests: distributional effects of later retirement; whether projected savings are realistic; how a funded pension pillar would be capitalised; and whether spending cuts can be delivered without reducing service quality.
dossier.open: A complete 2027 manifesto and costings; how he would assemble a parliamentary majority; details of funded pensions and transition protections.

principles: Non-partisan; no endorsement of candidates or parties.
Primary sources take precedence for what a candidate or party says about itself.
Independent reporting is used for context, scrutiny and corroboration, not substituted for primary evidence when the latter is available.
No position is inferred from party family, ideology, past manifesto or another politician.
Unknown, disputed, outdated and unverified claims are labelled and excluded from candidate matching where appropriate.
Corrections are logged with the previous wording, revised wording, date and reason.
source_hierarchy: Official candidate campaign website, signed programme, dated speech or direct interview recording/transcript.
Official party website and party programme, clearly labelled as party rather than personal candidate commitment.
Government, Parliament, Constitutional Council, courts, official statistics and regulatory institutions.
Independent reporting from multiple reputable French and international outlets.
Polling institutes and legally filed poll notices; secondary poll trackers are discovery aids only.
Commentary, aggregators and social media are leads, not sufficient proof for contested factual claims.

verification_statuses.meaning: Primary source checked and material details independently corroborated where practicable.

verification_statuses.label: Primary source checked

verification_statuses.label: Partially verified
verification_statuses.meaning: Some elements are supported, but material details, context or date remain unresolved.

verification_statuses.label: Unverified
verification_statuses.meaning: Insufficient evidence. Must not be presented as established fact or used in compass scoring.

verification_statuses.label: Outdated
verification_statuses.meaning: A once-valid statement has been superseded or is not evidence of a current 2027 position.

claim_rules: Every material policy claim should carry a source URL, source type, publication or statement date, date checked, and a concise context note.
Separate candidate statement, party programme, government record, independent analysis and editorial inference.
For numerical claims, verify units, baseline, timeframe and whether the number is a proposal, estimate or independently assessed result.
For legal or election-process claims, use the relevant official institution as primary source.
For polls, preserve pollster, sponsor, fieldwork dates, sample, method, question wording, candidate scenario and poll-notice link. Never compare unlike scenarios as if identical.
For disputed claims, record the competing evidence and do not silently choose a side.
News summaries must link to the original article, preserve attribution and avoid presenting analysis as fact.
editorial_standards.corrections_policy: Corrections are made transparently. Each correction records the date, affected page or claim, what changed, why it changed, and the sources supporting the revision. Material corrections should be visible to readers.
editorial_standards.compass_policy: The compass measures directional alignment only where a dated, attributable candidate position can be coded against a question. It does not infer positions from ideology. Missing positions are excluded from the score and displayed as evidence gaps. Match scores are not probabilities or voting recommendations.
editorial_standards.current_audit_limit: This is the launch of a formal editorial process, not a claim that every historical entry has already passed it. Legacy claims remain under audit until their individual verification records are completed.

source_provenance.source_id_rule: source_id is src- followed by the first 16 lowercase hexadecimal characters of SHA-256 of the exact cited URL.

source_provenance.verification_scope: Verification codes attach to claims or archived items, not to a publisher as a whole. A source citation alone does not establish verification.

compass_methodology.selection_rationale: The 12 areas cover core responsibilities of the French state and recurring subjects in the 2027 campaign: economy, taxation, pensions, immigration, security, healthcare, education, climate and energy, housing, Europe and institutions, foreign policy and defence, and rights and digital policy. This is an editorial framework, not a statistically representative ranking of voter priorities.
compass_methodology.question_rationale: Three questions per area provide breadth without allowing one policy area to dominate merely because it has more questions. Questions distinguish concrete policy choices and explain technical terms where needed.
compass_methodology.weighting: Each question receives a respondent-selected importance weight of 1, 2 or 3. Within each policy area, comparable question scores are first averaged using those weights. The area scores are then averaged equally, so each of the 12 areas has equal baseline influence. A user can leave a policy answer blank, but must rate the importance of every question.
compass_methodology.matching: Candidate positions are only scored when supported by dated, attributable evidence. Unknown positions are not inferred from party ideology or historical platforms. Missing evidence reduces coverage and is displayed. A match percentage is directional policy alignment, not a probability or voting recommendation.
compass_methodology.distance: For an ordinal question with N ordered answer positions, question alignment is 1 - absolute distance between respondent and candidate positions divided by N-1. Multi-dimensional or non-ordinal questions must not be forced into this scale; they require a separate explicit coding rubric.
compass_methodology.minimum_coverage: Do not publish a ranked percentage for a candidate unless evidence covers at least 6 of 12 policy areas and at least 12 questions. Otherwise show 'Insufficient comparable evidence' and list covered areas.
compass_methodology.status: Question framework complete. Candidate coding and primary-source verification remain incomplete. Existing hard-coded candidate positions must not be treated as verified evidence.
compass_methodology.review_note: The issue selection is informed by the scope of major public policy debates and comparison frameworks found in current French 2027 election coverage. It is not derived from polling about voter salience. Reassess topic balance as campaign programmes are published.
compass_methodology.default_design: Two questions from each of the twelve policy areas appear in the standard compass. One additional question per area is available in the optional extended stage.
compass_methodology.extended_design: The visitor may continue from the 24-question standard compass to answer the remaining twelve questions, bringing the total to 36.
compass_methodology.weighting_note: Policy areas retain equal baseline weight. Adding the third question in each area improves within-area detail; it does not increase that area’s overall baseline weight.

scoring_configuration.between_areas: unweighted mean across areas with comparable questions
